# Scientific review of the five-by-five bishop-placement homotopy classification

**Correctness — PASS.** The stated full-board face vector and both factor face vectors are independently generated by the exact bishop-attack predicate. All twelve tetrahedra are removed using verified free triangular faces. Contracting a spanning tree of each resulting two-complex gives a finite cellular presentation. Repeated valid generator/relator eliminations leave one and two circle generators, respectively, and five and three freely trivial two-cell attaching words. The join yields precisely \(2\) three-spheres, \(13\) four-spheres and \(15\) five-spheres. Exact integer Smith forms independently corroborate integral homology, without pretending that homology alone proves the homotopy result.

**Originality — PASS, qualified.** The source-inspected Ziegler shape theorems address shellability and skeleta; Shareshian–Wachs address complete and selected chessboard complexes; Clark–Zeckner study a restricted triangular Ferrers family whose all-positive-length condition does not include these two boards. The directly related bishop-independence publication treats maximum occupancy rather than homotopy, although only its abstract and metadata were available for inspection. Equivalent nonindexed work remains a bibliographic risk, and no search result proves uniqueness.

**Mathematical value — PASS.** The space is a canonical, finitely specified chess-piece placement complex rather than an arbitrary selected combinatorial slice. The full classification reveals three adjacent dimensions of sphere summands in a naturally nonpure configuration complex; the explicit two-color factorization and homotopy-preserving certificates explain the result rather than merely tabulating ranks. No claim about other board sizes or broader historical priority is made.

Self-review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.
